<observation>
  <type>bugfix</type>
  <title>Fixed UserCache.get concurrent null placeholder race in UserCache.java</title>
  <subtitle>Concurrent callers could both write a null placeholder; get now uses computeIfAbsent for atomic load-and-insert.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>UserCache.get now returns cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load) instead of cache.get(id)</fact>
    <fact>The previous cache.get(id) path allowed two concurrent callers to both write a null placeholder for the same id</fact>
    <fact>CacheConcurrencyTest passes after the change</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>The UserCache.get method previously returned cache.get(id), which allowed two concurrent callers to both write a null placeholder for the same id, producing a race condition. The method now returns cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load), which atomically loads and inserts the value so concurrent callers cannot both write a null placeholder. CacheConcurrencyTest passes.</narrative>

<observation>
  <type>bugfix</type>
  <title>Fixed UserCache.get race with computeIfAbsent in UserCache.java</title>
  <subtitle>UserCache.get now loads through computeIfAbsent so concurrent callers cannot both write a null placeholder.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>UserCache.get changed from `return cache.get(id);` to `return cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load);`</fact>
    <fact>computeIfAbsent guarantees only one caller invokes loader::load for a given id, preventing duplicate null placeholder writes</fact>
    <fact>CacheConcurrencyTest passes after the change</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>The UserCache.get method previously used `cache.get(id)`, which allowed two concurrent callers to both observe a missing entry and both invoke the loader, producing a race where both could write a null placeholder into the cache. Replacing the lookup with `cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load)` makes the load-and-put atomic: the first caller computes the value via loader::load while subsequent callers block or reuse the in-flight/resulting value, so only one write occurs per key. CacheConcurrencyTest confirms the concurrent scenario now resolves correctly.</narrative>
  <concepts>
    <concept>problem-solution</concept>
    <concept>pattern</concept>
  </concepts>

<observation>
  <type>bugfix</type>
  <title>Fixed ConnectionPool.borrow connection leak with try-with-resources</title>
  <subtitle>Connections are now closed when callers throw, preventing pool exhaustion.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>ConnectionPool.borrow in src/main/java/com/acme/db/ConnectionPool.java now uses try-with-resources to close the connection when the caller throws.</fact>
    <fact>PoolLeakTest reports activeConnections returns to 0 after 100 failing calls.</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>A connection leak in ConnectionPool.borrow was fixed by wrapping the Connection in a try-with-resources block. Previously, if a caller threw an exception while holding a borrowed connection, the connection was never returned to the pool, eventually causing pool exhaustion. The try-with-resources pattern guarantees the connection is closed regardless of how the caller exits. PoolLeakTest verifies the fix by asserting activeConnections returns to 0 after 100 consecutive failing calls.</narrative>

<observation>
  <type>bugfix</type>
  <title>Fixed token expiration boundary in JwtVerifier</title>
  <subtitle>JwtVerifier now rejects tokens whose expiration equals the current instant, closing an off-by-one acceptance window.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>JwtVerifier previously checked only `claims.getExpiration().before(now)`, so a token expiring at the exact current instant was accepted.</fact>
    <fact>The condition is now `claims.getExpiration().isBefore(now) || claims.getExpiration().isEqual(now)`, rejecting equality with the current instant.</fact>
    <fact>JwtVerifierTest#expiredAtExactBoundary passes with the new boundary condition.</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>JwtVerifier used a strict `before` comparison for token expiration, which accepted a token whose expiration timestamp was exactly equal to the verification instant. Because `before` is exclusive, that token was treated as valid at its own expiry moment. The verifier now also tests `isEqual(now)`, so any token whose expiration is not strictly in the future is rejected. The regression test `JwtVerifierTest#expiredAtExactBoundary` pins this boundary and passes.</narrative>

CounterServiceConcurrencyTest validates the fix by running 1000 concurrent threads and asserting the final counter value is 1000.</narrative>

The fix pins the charset to StandardCharsets.UTF_8 explicitly, making decoding deterministic regardless of the host JVM default. The regression test FileReaderFactoryTest#utf8FileKeepsAccents verifies that accented characters survive a full read on a GBK-default JVM, guarding against this platform-dependent pitfall.</narrative>
